correctness.rationale: For total labeled delegation functions, cycle labels and outside successor tree are uniquely reconstructed from positive-length reachability; reversal establishes exact profile bijection and every-fiber factor. The finite Cayley formula and SET species identity are derived, not assumed. Singularity analysis of \(T=z\exp(T)\) yields profile coefficients and shifted-Poisson law; the classical mapping connectedness EGF gives the distinct sampling contrast. The included checker exhaustively corroborates all functions through six vertices, separately from infinite analytic proof. Boundary \(n=1\) and terminal cycles of size 1 are handled.

Different terminology remains a historical-priority risk; novelty is qualified, not independently certified.

value.rationale: This identifies and quantitatively enumerates the voting input domain after collapsing observationally indistinguishable delegation networks, rather than merely recounting known labeled mapping graphs. The exact parameter-marked EGF, witnesses-per-profile formula and qualitative shift from a bounded shifted-Poisson to vanishing connectedness under alternative sampling conventions resolve a motivated question about synthetic peer-selection elections and information loss from delegations to observed ballots. No broader social interpretation is asserted.
